query: European Commission DMA non-compliance decision against Google Search Article 6(5) self-preferencing July 2026 - has a formal decision been adopted or announced? Latest status as of mid-July 2026
answer:
## Summary

**Yes — a formal decision has been adopted.** The European Commission formally adopted and announced its DMA non-compliance decision against Google on **23 July 2026**, resolving the "imminent" status that had characterized mid-2026 reporting.

**Key findings on the Article 6(5) self-preferencing matter:**
- **€460 million fine** specifically for self-preferencing Google's own services (Shopping, Hotels, Flights, transport, sports results) in Google Search, in breach of **DMA Article 6(5)**.
- Part of a **combined €890 million** in two separate decisions (the other €430 million was for Google Play anti-steering).
- **First-ever DMA fine against Google** and the **largest DMA penalty to date**.
- Google ordered to comply within **60 days** (Search redesign); non-compliance risks periodic penalties up to **5% of average daily worldwide turnover**.
- Official source: Commission press release **IP/26/1670**.
- Google may appeal to the EU General Court; no appeal confirmed filed as of reporting.

All core facts were cross-validated across the official European Commission DMA portal and multiple independent legal/trade outlets. A minor date discrepancy exists (one source cites 22 July internal adoption vs. 23 July public announcement), and the Commission PDF fetch returned some parsing artifacts that were corrected against the official web page.
